summary: Every checkable claim in the report matches the evidence: the build, rendering, images, MCP-only process, desktop/mobile verification and the template limitation. The only thing it leaves out is one minor convention issue (a repeated image on the front page), which isn't breakage.

claims.claim: Built The MCP Journal with a front-page listing and two published posts
claims.evidence: check.json: content.twoBlogPosts finds 2 posts, site.frontPageLinksPosts links 2/2 and content.allPublished passes. The front-page screenshot shows the 'Notes from a connected world' listing with two cards.

check.json: site.usesBlockGrid and schema.blockGridOnPages (blogFrontPage, blogPost) pass. It also has 3 adapters and 3 view components (Hero, PostListing, RichText). grade.md confirms the adapter → ViewComponent pipeline.

check.json: content.mediaFromProvidedPhotos shows 2 of 2 media files are the provided photos, and site.imagesFromMediaLibrary finds 0 hot-linked images. The crawl assets are all /media/... URLs. Photo credits are visible in the screenshots.

claims.claim: All content was created through MCP; no migrations were added
claims.evidence: check.json: process.intendedChannel says 'built through mcp' and code.noMigrationsWritten passes.

claims.claim: View it at https://localhost:44317/. Umbraco is running.
claims.evidence: No artifact records that port. site.boots and site.frontPage200 pass in the checker's own run.

claims.claim: Builds and desktop/mobile browser checks passed, including navigation and images
claims.evidence: check.json: build.ok shows 0 errors and 0 warnings, site.imagesLoad 4/4, and all 3 pages return 200. The changes list contains artifacts/*-1440.png and *-390.png for every page, which shows that desktop and mobile checks were actually run.

No breakage is visible in the pages, screenshots or checks. The only failing check is content.noRepeatedImages (usb-cables.jpg appears twice on index.html). That is a content-variety convention, not breakage, and the grader treats it as minor.

claims.claim: MCP template validation rejects Razor `?` operators, so the layout was saved locally
claims.evidence: grade.md: blogLayout was created via MCP, and its Razor was saved as a file because the MCP tool rejects `?`.

claims.claim: uSync exports are present; folder isn't a Git repository
claims.evidence: check.json changes.added lists many uSync/v18 configs. The environment is not a git repository.
